'''Vivienne Joyce Thom''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AM}} (born 1960) is an Australian former public servant and current independent consultant and intelligence specialist. From 2010 to 2015, Thom was the [[Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security (Australia)|Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security]] with oversight over the six agencies of the [[Australian Intelligence Community]].

== Biography ==
Thom has a doctorate and academic background in chemistry, and after post-doctoral work and teaching in the field, she joined the [[Australian Public Service]] as a patent examiner and qualified as a patent attorney.<ref name="csg">{{cite web |title=Our people: Dr Vivienne Thom AM |url=https://www.csg.org.au/our-people/#viviennethom |publisher=Centre for Strategy and Governance |access-date=22 June 2020}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1999, Thom was appointed as Commissioner of Patents and Registrar of Designs for [[IP Australia]]. From 2002 to 2006, she was Controller of the [[Royal Australian Mint]]. In March 2006, she joined the Office of the [[List of Australian Commonwealth Ombudsmen|Commonwealth Ombudsman]] as one of two Deputy Ombudsmen.<ref name="commomb">{{cite web |title=16 Feb 2006: Dr Vivienne Thom joins the Commonwealth Ombudsman's office |url=https://www.ombudsman.gov.au/media-releases/media-release-documents/commonwealth-ombudsman/2006/45 |website=www.ombudsman.gov.au |publisher=Commonwealth Ombudsman |access-date=22 June 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In 2010, she replaced [[Ian Carnell]] as Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security, serving in the role for five years. Since the end of her term as Inspector-General, Thom has worked as an independent consultant in the fields of integrity and governance in public administration.<ref name="csg" /> In 2019, Thom commenced an investigation into the conduct of former [[High Court of Australia|High Court]] Justice [[Dyson Heydon]], which found in 2020 that Heydon had repeatedly sexually harassed several judge's associates who worked for him.<ref name="heydon">{{cite news |title=High Court inquiry finds former justice Dyson Heydon sexually harassed associates |url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/high-court-inquiry-finds-former-justice-dyson-heydon-sexually-harassed-associates-20200622-p5550w.html |access-date=22 June 2020 |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=22 June 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In 2020, Thom was appointed to review [[Australian Securities and Investments Commission|ASIC]]'s governance following revelations that ASIC Chair James Shipton and Deputy Chair Daniel Crennan QC had received ASIC approved expense allowances for relocation. Both were cleared of any wrongdoing in Thom's report to Treasury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ministers.treasury.gov.au/ministers/josh-frydenberg-2018/media-releases/outcomes-review-asic-governance|title=Outcomes of review of ASIC Governance &#124; Treasury Ministers}}</ref>

== Accolades ==
In the [[2016 Queen's Birthday Honours (Australia)|2016 Queen's Birthday Honours]], Thom was made a [[Member of the Order of Australia]] for significant service to public administration through a range of senior roles, and as a mentor to women in executive positions.<ref name="am2016">{{cite web |title=Dr Vivienne Joyce THOM |url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1153830 |website=Australian Honours Search Facility |publisher=Australian Government |access-date=22 June 2020}}</ref>

== Oral history ==
Thom was interviewed in 2017 by Daniel Connell. The recording can be found at the [[National Library of Australia]].<ref>Thom, V.; Connell, D. (interviewer) (2017). [https://catalogue.nla.gov.au/catalog/7501399 ''Vivienne Thom interviewed by Daniel Connell in the IGIS oral history project''], National Library of Australia. Retrieved 28 April 2026.</ref>
